findings.issue: The app stays on the pre-Cache Components model (force-dynamic + fetch caching) while Next.js 16.4 (Oct 2026) now recommends Cache Components as the best choice for every app and new create-next-app apps ship with it enabled; it becomes the default in Next 17.
findings.suggestion: No action needed for stability today — the old model is fully supported in 16.x — but plan a migration to cacheComponents (use cache / cacheLife) before the Next 17 upgrade, when route segment configs like dynamic are replaced.

findings.issue: Exact pin 'next': '16.4.3' rather than a caret range; combined with the repo's zero-experimental posture this is consistent, but it can silently miss the scheduled November 2026 security release.
findings.suggestion: Consider '^16.4.3' or a lockfile-based update cadence so security patches land.

summary: This app has a zero-experimental footprint: exact-pinned stable Next 16.4.3 and React 19.3.1, no config flags, no unstable_/preview APIs, and only App Router primitives that have been stable since Next 13-15. Async params/searchParams are used correctly per the Next 16 breaking-change requirements. Upgrade risk is essentially nil; the only forward-looking gap is not adopting the now-recommended Cache Components model ahead of Next 17.
